Call (818) 548-4013 for program schedules. For public comments and questions during the
meeting, call (818) 937-8100. Public comments on a specific agenda item will be taken when that

assistance, please contact the City Clerk at (818) 548-2090 during regular business hours.
  PLEASE TURN OFF CELLULAR PHONES WHILE INSIDE THE MEETING LOCATION
In compliance with the Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) of 1990, auxiliary hearing aids, sign
language translation, and Braille transcripts are available upon request. Assisted listening devices
are available same-day upon request. The City Clerk’ office should be notified 72 hours (three
business days) or as soon as practicable for requests regarding sign language translation and
Braille transcription services. All documents related to open session items on this agenda that are
received less than 72 hours prior to this meeting, and are public records, will be available for review
in the Office of the City Clerk, 613 E. Broadway, RM 110, Glendale, CA 91206.
Translation services are provided for meetings through the use of bilingual staff for speakers who
wish to utilize the service as available. Speakers should state their request by contacting the City
Clerk’s office at (818) 548-2090, at least 72 hours prior to the scheduled meeting or as soon as

  SEPTEMBER 24, 2025 AT 9:30 AM

  1. ITEM:
  1719 GLADYS DRIVE
  SETBACK AND STANDARDS VARIANCE CASE NO. PVAR-003539-2024 &
  ADMINISTRATIVE EXCEPTION CASE NO. PAE-005000-2025

  PROJECT DESCRIPTION

  1
   The applicant is requesting Setback and Standards Variances and Administrative
  Exceptions to construct a 2,216 square-foot (SF), three-story single-family home with an
  attached two-car garage on a vacant 5,234 square-foot, hillside lot in the “R1R-
  I” (Restricted Residential Zone, Floor Area Ratio District I)., described as Lot 17, Block N,
  Tract No. 7600. Setback and Standards Variances are requested to develop the project on
  a substandard lot size (5,234 SF whereas 7,500 SF is required), for increased floor area
  (2,216 SF proposed whereas 1,572 SF is allowed), for reduced street front setback (5'-6"
  proposed whereas 15 feet is required), a reduced driveway length (minimum 5'-6" proposed
  whereas 18 feet is required). Administrative Exceptions are requested to exceed the
  maximum allowed height (38 feet proposed whereas 35 feet is allowed) and for reduced
  interior setbacks (minimum 7'-9" proposed whereas 10 feet is allowed).

  ENVIRONMENTAL DETERMINATION
  This project is categorically exempt from environmental review as a Class 3 “New
  Construction or Conversion of Small Structures” per Section 15303(a) of the State CEQA
  Guidelines because the project involves construction of one single-family residence on a lot
  zoned for single-family residential use.

2. ITEM:
  236 NORTH CENTRAL AVENUE AND 212 WEST CALIFORNIA AVENUE
  DENSITY BONUS REVIEW CASE NO. PDBP-001629-2023

  PROJECT DESCRIPTION
  An application for a Density Bonus Housing Plan to construct a new 8-story, 655,418
  square-foot, Mixed-Use Building that includes 682 residential units located at 236 North
  Central Avenue and 212 West California Avenue (the “Project”). The Project would contain
  a total of 72 residential units affordable to very low- and low-income households. The
  applicant is requesting two concessions/incentives to deviate from the proportionality
  requirements for inclusionary units and exceed the maximum floor area ratio (FAR); and
  four waivers to reduce the required amount of publicly accessible open space (PAOS),
  contiguous PAOS, residential private outdoor open space, and the requirement of a 20 foot
  setback for portions of the building wall over 60 feet in height and adjacent to the paseo.
  The existing 176,629 square-foot three-story retail building (former Sears Department
  Store), 164,308 square-foot three-level parking structure and a small asphalt surface
  parking lot will be demolished. The Project site is a 3.7 acre site located south of West
  California Avenue and east of North Central Avenue and west of North Orange Street
  consisting of four parcels (APNs: 5642-015-045, 5642-015-056, 5642-015-057, and 5642-
  015-058, addressed as 236 North Central Avenue) which is bisected by a 18 foot wide
  public alley (alley 239 proposed to be relocated onsite), located in the Downtown Specific
  Plan - Orange Central District. The project qualifies for reduced parking under the State
  Density Bonus Law and GMC 30.36.090. The project will provide a total of 930 parking
  spaces (one above grade and two levels subterranean).

  ENVIRONMENTAL DETERMINATION
  On June 30, 2025, budget trailer bills AB 130 and AB 131 were signed and took effect
  immediately. AB 130 added Public Resources Code Section 21080.66 creating a new
  statutory CEQA exemption for certain qualifying infill housing projects that meet the
  2
 following criteria:• Project site is no more than 20 acres.• Project site is within the
boundaries of an incorporated municipality, or "urban area" as defined by the U.S. Census
Bureau.• Project site was previously developed with "urban uses" or is substantially
surrounded by sites developed with urban uses.• Project is consistent with local zoning
standards, applicable general plan standards and any applicable local coastal program,
subject to deviations allowed by the State Density Bonus Law.• Project must be at least half
the density deemed appropriate to accommodate lower-income households in the State
Housing Element Law, as set forth in Gov. Code section 65583.2(c)(3)(B)• Project will not
require demolition of a historic structure that was placed on a historic register before the
project's preliminary application was submitted.• For projects submitted after Jan. 1, 2025,
no portion of the project will be used as a hotel, motel, or bed and breakfast.• All project
sites must satisfy SB 35's site eligibility criteria (farmland, wetlands and
conservation/species habitat areas are excluded, and coastal sites, fire hazard zones,
hazardous waste sites, earthquake fault zones and flood areas are subject to specified
restrictions).Staff has reviewed the project and has determined that it meets the criteria and
is statutorily exempt from CEQA review per Public Resources Code Section 21080.66

GLENDALE PLANNING HEARING OFFICER
 GLENDALE COMMUNITY DEVELOPMENT DEPARTMENT
  PUBLIC HEARING MINUTES
  SEPTEMBER 24, 2025
 9:30 a.m.  Mr. Roger Kiesel, Planning Hearing Officer, opened the hearing in Room
  105 of the Municipal Services Building. He outlined the requirements of
  Title 30 for the pertinent cases and described the provisions for appeal in
  Title 30 of the Glendale Municipal Code as well as the procedures for the
  conduct of the hearings.

  Mr. Kiesel announced that the agenda for the meeting was posted
  on September 17, 2025, at the City Hall Entrance.

 Staff Members Present – Community Development Department
 1) Mr. Roger Kiesel, Planning Hearing Officer
 2) Mr. Dennis Joe, Principal Planner
 3) Mr. Nik Hlady, Senior Planner

(1) LOCATION: 1719 GLADYS DRIVE
  ➢ SETBACK & STANDARDS VARIANCE CASE NO. PVAR-003539-2024
  ➢ ADMINISTRATIVE EXCEPTION CASE NO. PAE-005000-2025

 APPLICANT:  Juan Barbieri, Heritage Group, Inc.

 ZONE:  “R1R I” – Restricted Residential Zone, FAR District I

 LEGAL DESCRIPTION:  Lot 17, Block N, Tract No. 7600

 PROJECT DESCRIPTION
 The applicant is requesting Setback and Standards Variances and Administrative
 Exceptions to construct a 2,216 square-foot (SF), three-story single-family home
 with an attached two-car garage on a vacant 5,234 square-foot, hillside lot in the
 “R1R-I” (Restricted Residential Zone, Floor Area Ratio District I).

 CODE REQUIRES
 Standards Variances
 1) The minimum lot size for new residential development in the R1R zone is 7,500 sq.ft.
 2) The maximum allowable floor area ratio (FAR) in the R1R I zone is .30 (1,572 sq.ft.)

 Setback Variance
 1) The minimum required street-front setback for a new fence is 15 ft. in the R1R Zone.

 Administrative Exceptions
 1) The maximum allowable height in the R1R zone is 35 feet.
 Planning Hearing Officer Minutes  2
September 24, 2025

2) The minimum required interior setback in the R1R zone is 10 feet.

APPLICANT’S PROPOSAL
Standards Variances
1) To construct a single-family residence on the 5,234 square-foot lot.
2) To construct a single-family residence with a FAR of .42 (2,216 square feet).

Setback Variance
1) To construct a single-family residence with a minimum 5’-6” front setback.

Administrative Exceptions
1) To construct a single-family residence with a maximum height of 38 feet.
2) To construct a single-family residence with a minimum interior setback of 7’-9”.

ENVIRONMENTAL DETERMINATION
This project is categorically exempt from environmental review as a Class 3 “New
Construction or Conversion of Small Structures” per Section 15303(a) of the
State CEQA Guidelines because the project involves construction of one single-
family residence on a lot zoned for single-family residential use.

Staff
- Mr. Nik Hlady, Senior Planner and case planner on the proposed project,
overviewed the staff report. He answered questions from the Planning Hearing Officer.

Applicant
- Ms. Vicki Barbieri, architect and project consultant on the project, and representing the
owner, presented the proposed case. She answered questions from the Planning Hearing
Officer.
WRITTEN PUBLIC INPUT: None.//////////////////// GET FROM NIK

SPEAKING AT THE HEARING
In Favor:  No one.
In Opposition:  No one.
Interested Party: J.Edwards-neighbor / D.Caughan-neighbor / T.&S.Joyner-
  neighbors.

CALLERS:  None.

◼Rebuttal by the applicant Ms. Barbieri. She addressed concerns from neighbors.

The cases were taken under submission for a decision to be made at a later date.
   Planning Hearing Officer Minutes  3
  September 24, 2025

  (2) LOCATION: 236 NORTH CENTRAL AVENUE, AND
  212 WEST CALIFORNIA AVENUE
  ➢ DENSITY BONUS REVIEW CASE NO. PDBP-001629-2023
  (SEARS PROJECT)

APPLICANT:  Maple Multi-Family Land CA, LP, a Delaware limited partnership

ZONE:  “DSP/OC” - (Downtown Specific Plan - Orange Central District)

LEGAL DESCRIPTION:Portion of Lots 1-9 & 17-24
  (APNs: 5642-015-045, 5642-015-056, 5642-015-057, and 5642-015-058)

PROJECT DESCRIPTION
An application for a Density Bonus Housing Plan to construct a new 8-story, 655,418
square-foot, Mixed-Use Building that includes 682 residential units located at 236
North Central Avenue and 212 West California Avenue (the “Project”). The Project
would contain a total of 72 residential units affordable to very low- and low-income
households. The applicant is requesting two concessions/incentives to deviate from
the proportionality requirements for inclusionary units and exceed the maximum floor
area ratio (FAR); and four waivers to reduce the required amount of publicly
accessible open space (PAOS), contiguous PAOS, residential private outdoor open
space, and the requirement of a 20 foot setback for portions of the building wall over
60 feet in height and adjacent to the paseo. The existing 176,629 square-foot three-
story retail building (former Sears Department Store), 164,308 square-foot three-level
parking structure and a small asphalt surface parking lot will be demolished. The
Project site is a 3.7 acre site located south of West California Avenue and east of
North Central Avenue and west of North Orange Street consisting of four parcels
(APNs: 5642-015-045, 5642-015-056, 5642-015-057, and 5642-015-058, addressed
as 236 North Central Avenue) which is bisected by a 16 foot wide public alley (alley
239 proposed to be relocated onsite), located in the Downtown Specific Plan - Orange
Central District. The project qualifies for reduced parking under the State Density
Bonus Law and GMC 30.36.090. The project will provide a total of 930 parking spaces
(one above grade and two levels subterranean).

  ENVIRONMENTAL DETERMINATION
  On June 30, 2025, budget trailer bills AB 130 and AB 131 were signed and took
  effect immediately. AB 130 added Public Resources Code Section 21080.66
  creating a new statutory CEQA exemption for certain qualifying infill housing
  projects that meet the following criteria:

•  Project site is no more than 20 acres.
•  Project site is within the boundaries of an incorporated municipality, or "urban
  area" as defined by the U.S. Census Bureau.
•  Project site was previously developed with "urban uses" or is substantially
  surrounded by sites developed with urban uses.
   Planning Hearing Officer Minutes  4
  September 24, 2025

•  Project is consistent with local zoning standards, applicable general plan
  standards and any applicable local coastal program, subject to deviations
  allowed by the State Density Bonus Law.
•  Project must be at least half the density deemed appropriate to accommodate
  lower-income households in the State Housing Element Law, as set forth in
  Gov. Code section 65583.2(c)(3)(B)
•  Project will not require demolition of a historic structure that was placed on a
  historic register before the project's preliminary application was submitted.
•  For projects submitted after Jan. 1, 2025, no portion of the project will be used
  as a hotel, motel, or bed and breakfast.
•  All project sites must satisfy SB 35's site eligibility criteria (farmland, wetlands
  and conservation/species habitat areas are excluded, and coastal sites, fire
  hazard zones, hazardous waste sites, earthquake fault zones and flood areas
  are subject to specified restrictions).

  Staff
  - Mr. Dennis Joe, Principal Planner and case planner on the proposed project,
  overviewed the staff report. He answered questions from the Planning Hearing Officer.
  Staff has reviewed the project and has determined that it meets the criteria and is
  statutorily exempt from CEQA review per Public Resources Code Section 21080.66.
  = Mr. Mark Berry, also overviewed the details of the project.

  Applicants
  - Mr. Chris Burt, applicant and representing the owner, presented the case.
  - Mr. R. Pettersen – representative of the project’s applicant called and gave
  further details of the project.

  WRITTEN PUBLIC INPUT: Ms. F. Smith

  SPEAKING AT THE HEARING
  In Favor:  No one.
  In Opposition: No one.

  Interested Party: Ms. B. Brooks / Ms. L. Morris / Ms. F. Smith

  CALLER: Mr. Damian

  ◼Rebuttal by applicant. He addressed concerns from neighbors.

  The case was taken under submission for a decision to be made at a later date.

  The meeting adjourned at 12:45 p.m.

September 24, 2025
